desc: The famous columns of cold gas and dust inside the Eagle Nebula, photographed by Hubble in 1995 and again by JWST. The tallest pillar is about 4 light-years long; new stars are forming in their tips.
Stellar association that includes most of the Big Dipper stars, moving together through space.
The nearest OB association, a vast group of young hot stars spanning Scorpius, Lupus, Centaurus and Crux.
The stellar association containing Orion's Belt and Sword and the Orion Nebula.
The nearest large galaxy cluster, with 1,300 to 2,000 galaxies, dominated by M87. The Local Group is falling toward it.
Second-richest galaxy cluster within 100 million light-years, centred on NGC 1399.
Rich galaxy cluster of over 1,000 galaxies. Fritz Zwicky first inferred dark matter here in 1933.
One of the most massive objects in the nearby universe, the brightest galaxy cluster in X-rays, centred on NGC 1275.
Massive cluster near the centre of the Great Attractor, the gravitational anomaly pulling the Local Group and thousands of galaxies.
Galaxy cluster centred on NGC 4696, part of the Hydra-Centaurus Supercluster.
Galaxy cluster of about 160 bright galaxies in Hydra.
The largest concentration of galaxies in the nearby universe, containing over 8,000 galaxies.
The first quasar identified (1963) and the optically brightest. A supermassive black hole 2.4 billion light-years away, 4 trillion times as luminous as the Sun.
A vast empty region at least 150 million light-years across bordering the Local Group.
